title: CFD-002: the return motion—and the next rise.
summary: New pitch and heave minima mark the end of the first return motion. The hull is rising and rotating bow-up again; damping and stability remain undetermined.
evidence: Work in progress · simulated transient motion
heroAlt: Saved heave and pitch histories show new local minima followed by renewed upward and bow-up motion.
heroCaption: Work in progress — H0-CFD-002 dynamic simulation. 13,638 accepted saved motion samples through tau = 0.672907 s; no smoothing. Gold markers identify interpolated velocity-zero crossings. Results are transient, not final validated performance data.

sections.title: The return motion reaches new turning points
sections.text: Following the first motion reversals recorded on 8 October, the saved history now confirms a pitch minimum of approximately 10.026° bow-up at tau ≈ 0.555737 s. A later heave minimum occurs at tau ≈ 0.620103 s, approximately +77.392 mm above the release position. Pitch then increases again, and the hull resumes rising after its heave minimum.

sections.title: What changed since the first rise
sections.text: The first heave maximum was approximately +87.747 mm at tau ≈ 0.438109 s. The descent to the new minimum spans approximately 10.355 mm. Pitch decreased from the first local maximum of 10.738° to 10.026°, a change of approximately 0.712°. These are measured portions of the simulated transient record, not established periodic amplitudes.

sections.title: The calculation is still moving
sections.text: At the dated snapshot endpoint, tau = 0.672907 s, heave is approximately +79.311 mm and absolute pitch 11.012° bow-up. Vertical velocity is approximately +0.08127 m/s and bow-up rate +12.603°/s. Pitch has already exceeded its first local maximum, but a second pitch maximum has not yet been confirmed. Comparing an unfinished excursion with the first peak does not establish sustained growth or porpoising.

sections.title: How to read the graph
sections.text: Heave is displacement relative to the motion-release position. Pitch is the absolute bow-up attitude, starting near 0.411°, rather than a zeroed pitch change. Tau is simulated time since release from the CFD-001 state at solver time 1.579983709 s; it is not elapsed computing time. Lines join accepted saved motion samples without smoothing. Event times are interpolated within saved-step brackets after five consecutive samples of each velocity sign confirm a crossing.

sections.title: What this does not establish
sections.text: The monitoring classification remains “STILL TOO EARLY TO CLASSIFY.” The initial heave minimum and the following minimum are approximately 0.550486 simulated seconds apart, but that single interval is not a validated oscillation period. Further corresponding peaks and troughs are needed to assess damping, persistence or growth. No final drag, settled running trim, stable-planing conclusion or competitor comparison follows from this snapshot.

sections.title: The model and its limits
sections.text: This continues the constrained heave-and-pitch study at the 20 km/h boundary-speed condition. The other four rigid-body degrees of freedom remain constrained. Dry-board mass and inertia are provisional inputs; this is not a rider-loaded physical test. Numerical verification, model assumptions and eventual physical validation remain part of interpreting the result.

sections.title: The next evidence to look for
sections.text: The next review will examine subsequent corresponding maxima and minima alongside forces, moments and numerical diagnostics. Reaching the configured tau = 0.95 s endpoint completes the planned interval; it does not automatically demonstrate equilibrium, convergence or validated performance. This dated follow-up preserves the earlier snapshot and will remain available when later findings are published.
